status: Prepared locally; exact-source native concurrency/full-schema CI pending; no hosted acceptance
checked: First successful verified-source admission retains job/actor/student/document/path/object/version/reviewed hash and first claim identity before provider IO; no document text or student context is copied.

Binding is immutable to ordinary UPDATE/DELETE, including owner DML. Three RESTRICT foreign keys preserve the job, document and student. Bound jobs cannot be deleted or retargeted through input_source, actor, student, type or ID.
Completion requires an admission committed in an earlier transaction and rechecks current claim, source, scan, privacy context and permissions. A missing binding cannot be invented at completion.

Manual later claims retain the same original tuple; this does not authorize retries. Concurrent admissions/completions, retarget/delete lock waits and stale stronger-isolation writers have native-only cases.

Direct binding access is revoked for anonymous, authenticated and service roles. Existing service-only RPC signatures and response schemas are preserved. The restricted metadata catalog discovers the new references without reading user rows.

local_disposable_sql.skips: Real PostgreSQL concurrency cases; not local concurrency proof.

rollout_gates: All fourteen proposals remain unapplied and outside the canonical 210 migrations. Prepare/review a coordinated migration and worker rollout before requesting separate hosted authorization.
Pause/drain and reconcile existing in-flight unbound summary jobs. There is no invented backfill: old work without a prior binding must fail completion.
Review indefinite job/document/student retention and maintenance implications. Stronger transaction isolation is rejected for summary changes; READ COMMITTED remains required.
limitations: No provider or Storage IO, job retry, expiry, cleanup, quota release or terminal resolution. Stored object metadata is not physical-byte or immutable-provider proof.

Direct service result/status writes, unrelated job types, provider cancellation, dynamic/external references and the full permission/reference writer graph remain outside this boundary. Current permission checks are not a durable permission lease.
Ordinary DML guards do not constrain a privileged owner disabling triggers, issuing DDL or TRUNCATE. No direct object-store foreign key is added.
Report-length polish and Parent Pilot / Pathway Snapshot remain deferred; the complete TF-01–TF-26 and six-milestone roadmap is retained.
